messages:
Alex: heads up — noticed a tail-latency regression in prod for small-batch streaming paths after the fused-attn epilogue change. digging in now, filing notes here so we don't lose context.

Maria: ugh, saw a spike last night on a handful of routes. load balancer shows more 95p latency but p50 looks fine. any quick hypotheses? :thinking_face:

Alex: early hypothesis: fused-attn + qkv-pack epilogue is winning for long sequences but appears to degrade when KV cache hits are high and batch sizes are tiny (batch=1 or 2). suspect memory traffic + suboptimal kernel chooser decision.

Sanjay: can you paste profiler snippet? warp occupancy / l2 / dram counters would help.

Alex: pasted a short perf dump from a suspect RPC below (A100, seq=32, batch=1, kv_hit=true). key lines: 
```
--- perf-sample ---
Kernel chosen: fused_attn_epilogue_v2
SM utilization: 42%
DRAM throughput: 340 GB/s (peak 900 GB/s)
L2 hit rate: 28%
register spills: low
avg kernel time: 1.9 ms (attention compute)
KV cache lookup + copy: 0.9 ms
memset for output pad: 0.4 ms
--- end ---
```
Two things stood out: low SM utilization and relatively high DRAM usage vs L2. That pattern points to memory-bound small kernels.

Eva: interesting. contrast with a longer sequence case?

Alex: longer seq=1024, batch=4 on same hardware: fused_attn_epilogue_v2 shows SM util 78%, DRAM 600 GB/s, L2 hit rate 62%, kernel time 18 ms — overall good. So fusion helps when compute-to-memory ratio increases.

PerfBot: automated microbench results (summary):
- fused_attn_epilogue_v2: seq32,batch1: 2.9 ms total (net/RT)
- flash_attn_base: seq32,batch1: 2.1 ms total
- fused_attn_epilogue_v2: seq1024,batch4: 15.9 ms
- flash_attn_base: seq1024,batch4: 28.7 ms
(bench run: a100-40gb, driver 535.x, nvexp 23.6)

Maria: so fused wins on long, but loses on short. Kernel chooser currently picks fused whenever model supports epilogue fusion. That seems too aggressive.

Sanjay: agree. we need an adaptive chooser that looks at: sequence length distribution, batch size, kv_cache_hit_ratio, and observed p95 SLOs. Proposing threshold rules + a lightweight micro-profile on first N requests.

Alex: prototype config I tried locally:
```
{"kernel_chooser": {
  "default": "flash_attn_base",
  "rules": [
    {"if": "seq >= 256 || batch >= 4", "use": "fused_attn_epilogue_v2"},
    {"if": "kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.3 && seq >= 64", "use": "fused_attn_epilogue_v2"},
    {"else": "flash_attn_base"}
  ],
  "microprobe_samples": 8
}}
```
This reduced regressions in my local routing sim — but it's crude.

Eva: two follow-ups: (1) we should consider per-model historical seq distribution rather than single-request heuristics, (2) fallback latency penalty if we switch kernels mid-rollout.

Alex: yes. also need to account for hardware: H100 seems to push fused earlier because better L2 and bandwidth. PerfBot numbers on H100: fused seq32,b1 = 1.7 ms vs flash 1.9 ms (small win). so thresholds must be device-aware.

Maria: good call. can we add device fingerprint to the chooser and a tiny online estimator for L2-bandwidth effective? something like detect_hardware_profile() and use per-device cutpoints.

Sanjay: i'll draft a chooser PR that: (a) reads model seq histogram from recent traffic (last 5m), (b) queries device profile (A100/H100 via node metadata), (c) computes expected memory/compute ratio and picks kernel, and (d) logs decision + reason to tracing for later rollback.

Alex: logging the "why" is crucial. we kept that out of earlier rollout and it bit us. make reason strings short: e.g., "seq_hist_p95=512 -> fused", "device=A100 -> fallback flash", "kv_cache_hit=0.78 -> flash".

PerfBot: quick follow-up benchmark after Alex's config change on A100:
- route alpha (seq p95=40, batch mean=1.2): p95 latency reduced from 48ms -> 34ms after switching to flash_attn_base for that route.
- route beta (seq p95=800, batch mean=3.9): p95 unchanged (fused remains).

Eva: awesome. next ops steps? recommend:
1) Sanjay PR + perf tests (A100/H100) targeting canary hosts.
2) Add tracing keys: kernel_used, chooser_reason, seq_hist_p95, kv_cache_hit_ratio.
3) Add a rolling job that recomputes per-model cutpoints every 10m and emits an alert if >50% of requests flip kernel within 5m.

Maria: +1. also need a simple dashboard that surfaces routes with chooser flips and tail regressions (p95, p99). Without that we won't catch oscillations.

Sanjay: noted. I'll include a lightweight dashboard patch in the PR. planning to run perf matrix across seq in [16,32,64,128,256,512,1024] x batch in [1,2,4,8] x device in [A100,H100].

Alex: thanks all. last ask: Sanjay, can you run the matrix with kv_cache_hit_ratio toggled (0.9 vs 0.1)? that seems to be the other big factor. I'll coordinate with ops to deploy a canary route with the new chooser next week.

Sanjay: will do. I'll post the bench artifact link and a condensed decision table when finished.

Maria: :thumbsup: thanks — this explains the midnight pages for some product routes.

Alex: closing the loop after the PR lands. if anyone spots other weird regressions, drop here.

PerfBot: bench run queued: job_id=rb-2026-03-17-01. expected finish ~ 2h.
